alignments.note: Dative noun with no article and no determiner in the ASV, so the case preposition *by* stays with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause; discontinuous under rule 15.
Ordinary prohibitive negative with an expressed English *not*; rules 44 and 59 do not apply.
Imperative with its supplied auxiliary *Be* riding along under rule 9; head on the lexical verb *carried*, the particle *away* belonging to the English phrasal verb.
Verbless clause expressing no subject at all, so under rule 68 the predicate adjective carries both the supplied subject *it* and the copula; head on *good*.
Anarthrous dative with no determiner, so the case preposition *by* stays with the noun under rule 21.

Infinitive expanded into a finite clause; the supplied complementizer *that* belongs to the expanded complement under rule 85, not to `καλόν`, and the copula-auxiliary *be* rides along under rule 9. Head on the lexical *established*.

Anarthrous dative with no determiner; the supplied *by* stays with the noun under rule 21.
Portmanteau *wherein*: *where-* answers to the relative and *-in* to `ἐν`, so rule 35 makes this one `aligned` unit headed on the pronominal, not `noncompositional` under rule 45.
Negative with its own English *not*; the following verb is not a negative indefinite, so rules 41 and 59 do not empty it.
Aorist passive with its auxiliary *were* under rule 9; head on the lexical *profited*.
Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun *they* and nothing else under rule 32; the ASV writes two English words here, so rule 90's single-word case does not apply.

Participle rendered as a finite relative clause: the relativizer *that* is its helper under rules 7 and 32, and the reflexive *themselves* is required by the English idiom *occupied themselves*. Head on the lexical verb. Variant SBLGNT.HEB.13.9.v004 is underdetermined and the base reading `περιπατοῦντες` is compatible, so no textual decision is made here (rule 12).

review_notes: All 20 source and all 31 target ids partitioned exactly once.
Three dative nouns (s001, s009, s014) each keep their supplied case preposition because the ASV gives none of them a determiner and no article stands to anchor one (rule 21's determinerless clause).
The complementizer *that* was placed on the infinitive s010 rather than on `καλόν` per rule 85; rule 74's aside was considered and is scoped to a supplied subject, which does not arise here.
s015+s016 kept as one `aligned` unit for *wherein* under rule 35 rather than `noncompositional` under rule 45, since both elements are spelt in the English word.
s019/s020 split under rule 32: the ASV writes *they* and *that occupied themselves*, two English words, so rule 90's one-word relaxation is not in question.
